title: Strong coupling polarons in cavity quantum materials: limits of cavity-induced electron mass renormalization
abstract: Cavity-induced electron mass renormalization is an important ingredient of many proposals to control material properties through vacuum field modification. What is its ultimate limit? Here this question is answered by (i)~noting that this mass renormalization is essentially due to the field-mediated interaction between the electron and the polarizable degrees of freedom in the cavity mirrors, and (ii)~directly evaluating the corresponding Feynman path integral for a 2D electron by numerically exact quantum Monte Carlo. The sought upper limit is provided by the Landau-Pekar polaron in the planar geometry. The presented calculation bridges the gap between cavity control and dielectric engineering of material properties.
summary: This theoretical study calculates the maximum possible renormalization of an electron's effective mass when confined in a cavity due to coupling with polarizable material mirrors. By using advanced methods like Quantum Monte Carlo and variational calculations, the authors establish a definitive upper bound for this effect. This work bridges the gap between fundamental cavity QED theory and practical dielectric engineering of electronic materials.
main_problem: The paper aims to determine the ultimate theoretical limit for electron mass renormalization induced by coupling to the vacuum electromagnetic field within a planar cavity.
main_result: The upper limit for mass renormalization is found to be of the same order as the bulk Landau-Pekar polaron result, and the calculated dependence on system parameters is continuous, resolving previous debates about phase transitions.
method: The authors employ a combination of Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) evaluation of the Feynman path integral and variational minimization techniques applied to the polaron energy functional.
model_or_system: The system models a two-dimensional electron monolayer placed inside a planar cavity whose mirrors are described by a Lorentz oscillator dielectric function, leading to field-mediated electron-phonon interactions.
key_observables: Electron mass renormalization ($\Delta m/m$) and the polaron binding energy.
important_parameters: The dimensionless coupling strength ($\alpha_s$) and the normalized distance to the mirror ($\zeta = z_0 / \sqrt{2m\omega_s}$), which define the coupling regimes.
main_assumptions: The calculations assume the electrostatic (Coulomb) limit dominates at short distances, and the weak-coupling analysis assumes in-plane translation invariance.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical setup (planar cavity) and show comparisons of the calculated mass renormalization ($\Delta m/m$) versus the mirror distance ($\zeta$) using perturbative, QMC, and Landau-Pekar results.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical problem and model (2D electron in a cavity) to detailing the advanced computational methods (QMC, variational minimization) and finally presenting the results that establish the upper bound for mass renormalization.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses cavity QED effects on material properties, providing quantitative limits on how vacuum field modification can engineer electronic parameters like effective mass, which is central to AMO physics applications.
